sections.section_title: Modus Operandi of Fake Trading Apps and Social Media Groups
sections.content: Fraudsters create groups on social media platforms like WhatsApp and Telegram using names that resemble well-known SEBI registered intermediaries or foreign portfolio investors. Unsuspecting investors are added to these groups and lured with claims of high guaranteed returns, exclusive institutional trading access, and pre-IPO allocations.
key_takeaways: Unsolicited addition to WhatsApp/Telegram trading groups
Impersonation of SEBI-registered entities or FIIs
Promises of high or guaranteed returns

sections.section_title: Deployment of Unauthorized Mobile Applications and APKs
sections.content: Victims are instructed to download third-party applications via direct APK download links, unknown web URLs, or customized interfaces outside authorized app distribution stores. These fake applications simulate live market prices and display inflated fictitious trading profits on the user's dashboard to encourage larger deposits.
key_takeaways: Distribution via APK links or untrusted websites
Fabricated profit numbers displayed on simulated dashboards

sections.section_title: Routing of Funds to Third-Party and Mule Bank Accounts
sections.content: Payments for trading and margin deposits are solicited into personal bank accounts, third-party current accounts, or individual UPI handles rather than the designated registered client bank account of a recognized stockbroker.
key_takeaways: Deposits directed to personal bank accounts or arbitrary UPI handles
Absence of official designated client account routing

sections.section_title: Withdrawal Demands and Artificial Fee Traps
sections.content: When an investor attempts to withdraw funds or claimed profits, the perpetrators deny access, demanding additional payments under the pretext of statutory taxes, platform fees, conversion charges, or account unfreezing fees. Once the demand is met, further fees are demanded or communication is abruptly cut off.
key_takeaways: Refusal to process withdrawals without advance fees or taxes
Threat of account forfeiture to coerce further deposits

sections.content: SEBI reiterates that registered intermediaries never guarantee returns on stock market investments and never solicit funds into third-party accounts. Investors must verify registration status on the official SEBI website (www.sebi.gov.in) and download trading applications only from recognized app stores verified against registered brokers.
key_takeaways: No registered intermediary guarantees market returns
Always verify intermediary registration on sebi.gov.in
Report cyber fraud immediately to 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in
